text: You've spent this chapter so far on locks — the mechanism SQL Server uses to keep one transaction's in-progress work from corrupting another's. This lesson introduces isolation levels: how you control how much of that protection a given transaction actually gets.

You set it with one statement, SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL, naming the level you want. Every level makes the same trade-off at a different point on the dial. Stricter isolation means fewer anomalies and stronger correctness guarantees, but more blocking and less concurrency. Looser isolation means less blocking and more throughput, but more ways for a transaction to see data that's wrong or that shifts out from under it.

Every isolation level is defined by which of three classic anomalies it allows and which it prevents. A dirty read means reading another transaction's change before it's even committed. A nonrepeatable read means reading the same row twice and getting two different values. A phantom read means running the same query twice and getting a different set of rows entirely. The next three lessons take each one apart in full, with a concrete two-session timeline.

The SQL standard defines four levels, and SQL Server implements all four: READ UNCOMMITTED, the loosest; READ COMMITTED, which is SQL Server's default; REPEATABLE READ; and SERIALIZABLE, the strictest. Each one down that list prevents strictly more anomalies than the one before it, at the cost of more blocking.

SQL Server also adds two mechanisms built on row versioning instead of locking. SNAPSHOT is a session-level isolation level, set the same way as the four ANSI levels. RCSI, Read Committed Snapshot Isolation, is different — it's a database-wide setting an administrator turns on once, and it quietly changes what ordinary READ COMMITTED means for every query in that database, with no application code changes required.

That's the full map of this cluster: three anomalies, then six levels, then how to actually choose between them. Next lesson, we start with the first anomaly in full detail — the dirty read. See you there.
